summary.title: Building a search engine using Redis and redis-py
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a working full-text search engine with Redis sorted sets and sets in Python, using TF-IDF scoring via ZUNIONSTORE.
takeaways: Redis sets, sorted sets, and ZUNIONSTORE are enough to build an inverted index with TF-IDF ranking.
Parsing (lowercasing, alphanumeric filtering, stop words, short-word removal) matters most for search quality.
Pipelines reduce network round-trips when indexing and searching; the same function can add or remove documents.
Replacing TF with a constant 1 allows plain sets instead of sorted sets, saving memory.
Redis keeps data in memory, so very large indexes need more machines and sharding brings its own latency trade-offs.
summary.summary: The post walks through a minimal search engine built on redis-py. It covers a simple tokenizer with a stop-word list, an indexing function that stores term frequencies in per-term sorted sets and document IDs in a set, and a search function that computes IDF from ZCARD counts and combines scores with ZUNIONSTORE. The author then lists improvements such as query operators, using SDIFF for exclusions, and memory trade-offs, and notes that Redis's in-memory design limits index size. It also mentions that stemming and metaphone are optional and not used in the code.
